children: unit Genentech on Wednesday announced that the FDA has granted priority review to a marketing application for fenebrutinib, designed as an oral treatment for a central nervous system autoimmune condition called multiple sclerosis.
The new drug application seeks FDA approval of the Bruton’s tyrosine kinase inhibitor for both relapsing multiple sclerosis and the primary progressive form of multiple sclerosis.

The Swiss drugmaker already markets intravenously and subcutaneously delivered versions of its MS therapy, Ocrevus, as the current standard of care and the only approved medicine for PPMS, a condition affecting roughly 15% of MS patients.

The NDA is supported by data from three late-stage trials, including FENhance 1 and 2, in which fenebrutinib outperformed the standard of care, teriflunomide, in reducing relapses and both active and chronic brain lesions in MS patients.
